headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 6 studies yielded an overall effect size of 1.61 (95% CI: 1.18–2.18), suggesting that alpha-linolenic acid is associated with a higher risk of prostate cancer. However, this association should be interpreted with caution, as there was very high between-study heterogeneity (I² = 85.74%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
